chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Fadala from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
I asked: 'A man places his hand in prayer and folds the right over the left.' He said: 'That is the act of the Jews, so do not do it.'

key_terms.اَلتَّكْفِيرُ: The act of the Jews / Disbelief (contextually used as 'that is what the Jews do')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on folding hands during prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Sahih al-Tusi, the Imam identifies placing the right hand over the left during prayer as 'al-takfir' (disbelief or distinctiveness of the People of the Book), a ruling that distinguishes Shia practice from the Sunni tradition of folding hands (nafl). This emphasizes the Shia jurisprudential preference for keeping the hands hanging at the sides or slightly raised, reflecting a return to the Prophetic sunnah as interpreted by the Ahl al-Bayt.
